svg.title: Non-mechanical back and neck pain: a nerve squeezed at the side (radiculopathy) or in the centre (lumbar stenosis, cauda equina syndrome, cervical myelopathy), or everything else flagged by red flags (inflammatory, fracture, infection or neoplasm); each column gives presentation, investigations and treatment, with visceral causes and the no-red-flag starting treatment below

svg.text: Back or neck pain that is NOT just mechanical: where is the problem?

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: OLDCARS + red flags every time · first exclude non-spinal causes: hip, visceral, vascular, systemic, viral

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: nerve compression can come from ANYTHING: disc, spondylosis, abscess, tumour, bleed, slipped vertebra

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: primary-care triage: serious spinal disease < 1% · radicular pain, radiculopathy, stenosis 5-10% · non-specific 90-95%

svg.text: the cord ends at ~L1: lumbar stenosis squeezes ROOTS, cervical squeezes the CORD

svg.text: EVERYTHING ELSE: found by red flags

svg.text: red flag → plain films for fracture · MRI for neurological compromise, infection, neoplasm
